W5 (contrarian), after E060. Tip E060 5.178 s / 0.7533 (seeds 0-2 exactly at the bar).
1. Accuracy noise: per-seed SD ~0.25 pp, 3-seed SD ~0.15 pp, build component ~0 (E057/E059). A recipe with population ~0.7535 passes the 0.753 gate ~50%. The tip sits on the gate edge, so any lever costing >0.1 pp fails seeds 0-2 more often than not.
2. Time noise is the dominant unpriced term: identical code read 5.079 vs 5.193 (E046/E059) and 5.198/5.206/5.223 (E049 rebuilds). New mechanism (not only kernel reselection): session-level drift in host-side launch overhead with 4 pinned CPU cores, plus cudagraph pool placement, shifts all 3 trials together. So wall-time keeps under ~2% (E049 over E046, E060 over E049 at -0.4%) are mostly draws; small levers need CUDA-event per-step timing or repeated sessions. My time misses (E050, E056, E059) all fit this.
3. Accuracy is carried by optimizer steps on layers still learning: lowering early pixels at a fixed step count is free (E026, E033); removing steps costs at the dial (E031, E041, E045 inverse); freezes are free only after learning ends (whitening ~6% E060, stem 75%, g2 ~90%). Earlier freezes cost (E037 -0.4, E055 -0.15, E054 -0.48). Muon renormalizes filters, so filter update-rate curves are tautological with the LR schedule.
4. Per-step cost: resolution-independent work (3 Muon NS calls, fused SGD, Lookahead) weighs most at 20-24 px; freezes beat their FLOP share by skipping BN/GELU backward and Muon calls. E056: activation backward bytes matter, but only ReLU's mask-style backward saves them, and ReLU costs ~0.5 pp. tanh-GELU and SiLU still save the fp16 input, so little saving.
5. End-game at a local optimum (E025, E030, E032, E044 hurt). Remaining cheap levers are identical-math systems work: one batched NS graph, skipping NS for groups whose LR is ~0 during the anneal, fewer compiled variants.
6. Settled by reading the code: BN scale frozen, filter wd inert, only fine labels supplied.
7. Muon vs SGD: E006's gain is confounded; PR #3 favours SGD. At batch 2000 the SGD lr is untuned, and the freeze anneals interact with non-normalized filters, so I expect SGD to lose about 0.3-0.5 pp now and save ~0.14 s.
8. PCIe judge: times 5-10% higher.
Unsure about: the true cause of session time drift; whether Muon's advantage is real at batch 2000; how judge builds and times differ from local SXM4.

forecasts.reason: E041 saved ~0.05 s for 12 early steps and cost ~0.2 pp; early steps carry accuracy and are cheap in time.
Dropping 3 NS graphs saves ~0.14 s, but the SGD lr and its interaction with the freezes/anneal are untuned at batch 2000; expect a loss of at least 0.3 pp.
erf is cheap on A100; only ReLU's mask-style backward saves bytes, so the projected saving is probably <1.5% and the branch closes without a run (point = tip values).
Removes ~32 cheap but accuracy-carrying steps, the mirror image of E045 (+0.135 pp for more early steps).

cruxes: Is the ~2% wall-time spread between builds and sessions also present in per-step CUDA-event time? If not, the drift is host-side (CPU, launches), and wall-time rankings need repeated sessions.
With matched schedules, does SGD lose more than 0.25 pp to Muon on fresh seeds? That decides whether removing ~0.15 s of Newton-Schulz work pays.
How much of each step's time is Newton-Schulz plus optimizer launch overhead that one batched graph (identical math) could remove?
